items.followUp: Describe how water molecules interact with sodium and chloride ions when NaCl dissolves.

rubric.why: The oxygen end of a water molecule is partially negative and attracts the positive sodium ion.
rubric.description: States that the oxygen end of water attracts Na⁺ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attraction between the oxygen end of water and Na⁺.

rubric.why: The hydrogen end of a water molecule is partially positive and attracts the negative chloride ion.
rubric.description: States that the hydrogen end of water attracts Cl⁻ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attraction between the hydrogen end of water and Cl⁻.

modelAnswer: The oxygen end of water molecules attracts Na⁺ ions.
The hydrogen end of water molecules attracts Cl⁻ ions.

items.followUp: Write the equation for the reaction of methane with chlorine in bright sunlight.

rubric.why: One hydrogen atom in methane is replaced by a chlorine atom, producing chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.
rubric.description: Writes the correct balanced reaction equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the reactants and products CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.

rubric.why: Bright sunlight provides the condition for the reaction to occur.
rubric.description: States that the reaction takes place in bright sunlight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying bright sunlight or sunlight.

modelAnswer: The reaction takes place in bright sunlight.
